text: {"domains":{"block_M":[32,64,128],"block_N":[64,128],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3],"threads":[128]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1,"launches":1,"pipeline":1,"footprint":1},"rationale":"No prior configurations have been evaluated, so all listed domains are kept nonempty and the shared-memory cap is set to the portability cap of 32768 bytes. For M=128, N=4096, K=4096, block_M must divide 128, block_N must divide 4096, and block_K must divide 4096, so all domain values are feasible. Equal weights give a neutral initial objective across memory traffic, launch count, pipeline depth, and shared-memory footprint. The estimate uses max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N), with explicit epilogue barriers ensuring buffer aliasing; actual compiled memory is still checked. Next hypothesis: larger block_M and block_N should reduce traffic and launches, while stages and footprint trade off against pipeline efficiency within the 32KB cap. Validation scope: any Metal checks would execute the exact source/config/TIR, but no CUDA binary is executed; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements."}
